app.title: Computational Life Lab
app.summary: A person picks an experiment configuration and seed, or loads an earlier stored run from its last checkpoint, and then steps or plays the simulation forward one batch of epochs at a time. While it runs they watch a grid of the population, where repeated genomes are coloured, next to line charts of diversity, entropy and complexity proxies over epochs. As the run goes, the population is checked at intervals for candidate self-replicators, and every run is saved with its metrics, checkpoints and the epoch of the first detection. They can also open one organism to read its genome, instruction counts and lineage, score it, step through a paired execution by hand, scan a sample for the highest-scoring candidates, and overlay a metric across several stored runs.

task.text: Run a simulated population of self-modifying programs, watch its population statistics change, and spot and inspect candidate self-replicators when they emerge.

data.text: A population of fixed-length byte genomes evolving over epochs. Each run keeps a per-epoch history of metrics, an event log, saved checkpoints and, optionally, recorded parent–child lineage.
data.item: an organism: one fixed-length byte genome in the population, with its parents, generation and birth epoch

stage.text: running and watching simulation experiments, then analysing and comparing their runs

mechanism.text: Sidebar controls set up, load and advance the simulation. Each step redraws a population grid and the metric line charts, and an organism index drives a detail panel with its genome tape, instruction bar chart, lineage graph and a step-by-step execution debugger. A sample scan ranks candidates and can send the top one to the inspector, and a separate panel overlays one metric across chosen stored runs.

field.text: simulating self-replicating program soups in artificial life

steps.step: filter to the items that matter

choose a run database, multi-select stored runs and a metric, and overlay that metric's history across the runs on one line chart

distinctive: there is no fitness function: replication is only observed by a separate analysis heuristic (a genome is paired with random partners over chained generations) that never feeds back into the simulation
only repeated genomes are coloured in the grid, because an exact duplicate is astronomically unlikely by chance, so any repeat is a real signal against a grey background
every run is deterministic from its configuration and seed and is persisted from the start (metrics, events and periodic checkpoints), so a multi-day run can be resumed later from its checkpoint
ancestry is a DAG with two parents per organism, drawn by generation and truncated to the nearest relatives instead of forced into a single founder tree
a hand-stepped interpreter debugger shows the two heads and the program counter on the shared tape
